RABIES

 
 
 
 

 
 
Animal bites are REPORTABLE if any suspicion of Rabies 
MANAGEMENT OF ANIMAL/DOG BITES 
 
Risk assessment for post exposure prophylaxis 
• 
Unprovoked animal attack – dogs, cats, cattle, goats, horses, sheep, pigs, jackals, wild cat species, mongoose, 
seals, dassies (rock hyrax), squirrel, antelope, bats and others. NOT rats/mice/reptiles/birds. 
• 
Animal with unusual behaviour-aggressive, salivating, wild animal appearing tame, uncoordinated movements. 
• 
Category of bite. NB RIG is CRITICAL in head/neck/face wounds – short incubation period 
• 
SAFE in lactation & pregnancy, same dose 
 
Category of 
Exposure 
Type of Exposure 
Action 
Category 1 
• Touching or feeding animal 
• Licking of intact skin 
• No action if history of vaccination reliable 
• If hx of vaccination not reliable manage as 
category 2 
Category 2 
• Nibbling of uncovered skin 
• Superficial scratch NO SKIN 
BREACH, NO BLEEDING 
• Wound management 
• Rabies vaccine full course 
• Rabies immunoglobulin if immune-compromised 
Category 3 
• Bites or scratches that 
penetrate skin 
• Licking of mucous membranes 
• ANY contact with a bat 
• Wound management 
• Rabies vaccine full course 
• Rabies immunoglobulin 
 
General Wound Management 
• 
Flush well with soap and water 
• 
Clean with 0.05% chlorhexidine or 10% iodine 
• 
Avoid suturing and local anaesthetic agents 
• 
Antibiotics if indicated 
• 
Tetanus toxoid booster (TIG if severe wounds) 
 
Rabies Vaccine (Verorab) 
• 
1 Amp/ dose for adults and children 
• 
Course = day 0, 3, 7 and 14 
• 
IMI deltoid or anterolateral thigh (avoid the 
gluteus maximus) 
• 
If a dose is delayed, resume & complete 
regimen, do not restart regimen 
Rabies Immunoglobulin (Rabigam, Equirab) 
• 
20 IU/kg of human rabies immunoglobulin 
• 
40 IU/kg of equine rabies immunoglobulin 
• 
Can be given up to 7 days post administration 
of rabies vaccine, give ASAP 
• 
Infiltrate entire dose around/into the wound. 
Dilute with saline if more volume is needed for 
multiple wounds 
• 
BE AWARE: The risk of ANAPHYLAXIS is more 
common with equine than human rabies 
immunoglobulin 
i.e.  1:150,000 patients 
• 
Hence administer in setting with resuscitation 
equipment available. 
 
 
For advice on prophylaxis and medical issues: NICD 24-hour clinician hotline: 0800 212 552, or HJH ID Consultants 
Source: NICD Rabies Guidelines 2021 

 
The Dosage of Anti-Rabies immunoglobulin to be administered according to Body Weight 
ANTI-RABIES IMMUNOGLOBULIN 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
BE AWARE: 
The risk of ANAPHYLAXIS is more common with Equine immunoglobulin than Rabigam 
i.e. 1:150,000 patients DOSAGE = 40IU/kg 
(i.e. 2 x dose Rabigam but volume of Equine IG is 1,000IU/5mℓAnti-Rabies Immunoglobulin
